subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Framing Effect
description: A quick, practical guide to The Framing Effect.

hook.text: Would you prefer beef that is 75% lean or 25% fat? Same beef. Different frame. Different choice.

buildup.text: The framing effect: the way a choice is worded changes the decision—even when the options are identical.

discovery.text: Tversky and Kahneman showed that people choose surgery framed as "90% survival" over "10% mortality."

twist.text: Loss frames trigger risk-seeking. Gain frames trigger risk-aversion. The frame flips your strategy.

climax.text: Politicians, marketers, and lawyers engineer frames deliberately. The question is never neutral.

punchline.text: How you ask changes what they answer.

quiz.question: How does framing change decisions?
options: It changes how options are perceived without changing facts
